results.title: Ghanaian neuroscientist honoured at Millennium Excellence Awards USA for Alzheimer’s blood test discovery

results.title: Mahama appoints 15 officers of the Ghana Prisons Service
results.content: President John Mahama has promoted 15 officers of the Ghana Prisons Service, elevating seven Deputy Directors of Prisons to Directors of Prisons and eight Assistant Directors of Prisons to Deputy Directors of Prisons.

results.title: Minerals Commission defends termination of Northern Ashanti Mines’ mineral rights over $8.3m debt
results.content: The Minerals Commission has defended its decision to terminate the mineral rights of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited, formerly Owere Mines, insisting that the company persistently failed to meet its statutory financial obligations despite several opportunities to settle its debts.

results.title: Women domestic workers earn 48% of other employees’ wages – ILO
results.content: Women employed as domestic workers worldwide earn an average of 48% of the monthly wages of other employees, highlighting persistent gender-based inequalities in the sector, according to the International Labour Organization (ILO).

results.title: Africa records 4.2 million increase in domestic workers since 2019 – ILO
results.content: Africa recorded an increase of 4.2 million domestic workers between 2019 and 2025, the largest rise among the world's regions, according to the International Labour Organization (ILO).

results.title: Ghana at risk of missing 2030 methane emissions target, AMA warns, as stakeholders push for more funding and waste separation
results.content: Ghana risks missing its target of cutting methane emissions from the waste sector by 30 percent by 2030, officials of the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) have warned, citing funding shortfalls and weak waste collection. The warning came on Wednesday at the Accra LOW-M Institutional and Climate Finance Roundtable at the Africa Regent Hotel in Accra. The event was organised by the AMA and the Green Africa Youth Organization (GAYO), with the Global Alliance for Incinerator Alternatives (GAIA) and C40 Cities. It brought together the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, the Ministry of Finance, the Environmental Protection Agency and its Ghana Carbon Markets Office, the private sector and informal waste workers. results.content: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has rejected reports that it is considering changes to its parliamentary leadership, saying no discussions have taken place to replace Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin and his team.

results.title: GAYO, AMA hold roundtable to secure funding and institutional backing for Accra’s methane reduction plan
results.content: The Green Africa Youth Organization (GAYO) and the Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) have held a roundtable to get government institutions and funders to commit to Accra's plan to cut methane emissions from waste. The Accra LOW-M Institutional and Climate Finance Roundtable: Advancing Coordinated Action and Climate Finance for Urban Methane Reduction, held on Wednesday at the Africa Regent Hotel in Accra, focused on the Accra LOW-M (Lowering Organic Waste Methane) Portfolio. The plan aims to cut methane emissions from the city’s waste by at least 30 percent by 2030, mainly by turning organic waste into compost and biogas instead of sending it to landfills. results.title: More than 80% of domestic workers worldwide remain in informal employment – ILO
results.content: More than four in five domestic workers worldwide remain in informal employment, often without effective labour and social protection, despite progress in many countries, a new report by the International Labour Organization (ILO) has found.

results.content: Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh says the La General Hospital project, valued at €50 million, is expected to be completed by the end of 2027, with about €15 million paid so far.

results.content: Energy and Green Transition Minister Dr John Abdulai Jinapor has sworn in a reconstituted Board of BOST Energies Limited, charging members to strengthen corporate governance, improve operational efficiency and safeguard the company’s long-term sustainability.

results.title: Ghana plans local production of active pharmaceutical ingredients to cut drug imports
results.content: Ghana is planning to develop local capacity to manufacture active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), the key components responsible for the therapeutic effects of medicines, as part of efforts to reduce dependence on imported drugs.

results.title: Mahama says Ghana is in talks with Russia over first nuclear power station
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama says Ghana has initiated discussions with Russia’s state nuclear corporation, Rosatom, over the establishment of the country’s first nuclear power station. results.title: NPP introduces early eligibility checks for 2028 parliamentary aspirants at GH¢2,000 fee
results.content: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has introduced a GH¢2,000 fee for prospective parliamentary candidates, including sitting Members of Parliament (MPs), to declare their intention to contest the party’s primaries ahead of the 2028 general elections. The party’s General Secretary, Justin Kodua Frimpong, announced the measure at a press conference on Thursday, October 29, 2026, describing it as a first in Ghana’s political landscape. “The party, as usual, has always been the pace setter. And this is the first time that we are doing something of this sort in our political dispensation,” he said. The process is scheduled to run from November 1 to November 10, 2026, through the party’s designated portal, PPC.nppghana.org.

results.title: NPP sets November 1–10 for parliamentary aspirants to declare interest
results.content: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has scheduled November 1 to 10, 2026, for prospective parliamentary candidates, including sitting Members of Parliament, to formally declare their intention to contest the party’s parliamentary primaries ahead of the 2028 general elections. The party’s General Secretary, Justin Kodua Frimpong, announced the timeline at a press conference on Thursday, October 29, saying the declaration of intent would be the first step in the process leading to the primaries. He said the party would assess prospective candidates against its constitutional requirements and the laws of Ghana to determine their eligibility. “Our prospective parliamentary candidates will be checked on whether or not, per our constitution, they indeed qualify to stand as or to be nominated as a parliamentary candidate for our party,” he said.

results.title: Ghana’s pharmaceutical industry has entered its ‘golden era’ – NVI CEO
results.content: The Chief Executive of the National Vaccine Institute (NVI), Dr Sodzi Sodzi-Tettey, has declared that Ghana’s pharmaceutical industry has entered its “golden era” as the government launched a new policy framework on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

results.title: Driver suffers severe chemical burns after hydrogen peroxide truck catches fire at Goriyiri
results.content: A driver has sustained severe chemical burns following a fire and reported explosion involving a truck transporting 35 Intermediate Bulk Containers (IBCs) believed to contain hydrogen peroxide at Goriyiri in the Nadowli-Kaleo District of the Upper West Region.

results.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Strengthening the CEO’s Leadership Legacy
results.content: A CEO’s leadership legacy is not defined solely by financial results or personal achievements. It is also reflected in the strength of the institution left behind, the leaders developed, the culture established, the trust earned, and the organization’s ability to perform beyond the current leader’s tenure. Building a lasting legacy requires CEOs to make decisions that serve the organization’s long-term interests, develop people who can carry the mission forward, and strengthen systems that support continuity and accountability.

results.title: Fire outbreaks leave a trail of destruction at Bunso, Boso and Nsawam
results.content: Three separate fire outbreaks at Bunso, Boso and Nsawam in the Eastern Region have destroyed properties, including a generator, household items and a truck transporting goods, leaving two people injured.

results.title: Accra Metropolitan University postpones Dzenten Festival amid Tema-Nungua land dispute
results.content: Accra Metropolitan University has postponed the Dzenten Festival, scheduled for Sunday, November 1, 2026, citing security concerns arising from a dispute between the traditional authorities of Tema and Nungua over ownership of land and the Meridian Rock. In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, signed by Mr Ebenezer T. Hanson, Head of Public Relations and Communications at Accra Metropolitan University, the University said the decision was taken as a precautionary measure until the concerns surrounding the dispute had been addressed.
